phrases.latin: Lege mihi fābulam ex hōc librō!
phrases.english: Read me a story from this book!

phrases.latin: Narrā etiam ūnam, pater! — Estō, sed ūnam modo.
phrases.english: Tell me one more, Dad! — All right, but only one.

phrases.latin: Legit mihi nūper epistulās; uxōris esse dīcēbat.
phrases.english: He read me some letters recently; he said they were his wife’s.

phrases.latin: Sī interruptum somnum reciperāre … nōn posset, lēctōribus aut fābulātōribus arcessītīs resūmēbat.
phrases.english: If he could not get back to sleep once it was broken, he sent for readers or storytellers and so took it up again.

phrases.latin: Lavātus es; jam in lectulum, et fābulam narrābō.
phrases.english: You’ve had your bath; now into bed, and I’ll tell you a story.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
